checks: The integer bases are precisely the four extreme vertices of the binary square, so the hull's sampled fibers are exactly the unit intervals. For real base (s,t) the remaining barycentric weights after choosing weight w at 11 are s−w, t−w and 1−s−t+w; nonnegativity gives the stated closed range.

At fixed feasible weights the weighted sum of unit intervals has length one and lower endpoint Lw. Varying w over its interval gives the displayed fiber for all L≥0. The range length of w equals min(s,t,1−s,1−t), never exceeding 1/2 and attaining it at the square center. This gives W=1+L/2 and also covers L=0.

Every closed ambient halfspace containing an interval midpoint contains at least a half-interval in that fiber, including pure-base normals. For any point choose the nearer-endpoint side and use the affine binary distance, zero at its base and positive at every other sampled base, with a sufficiently large coefficient to exclude all other fibers. Hence the maximum depth is 1/2 in raw units and 1/8 normalized.

At budget 1/2 a nonvertical cap containing a midpoint has its plane through that midpoint and no other-fiber volume. Every cap missing the midpoint has a strict margin gap there, so finitely many such caps miss a neighborhood. The two signs must therefore both be present through every midpoint. A cap cannot contain two midpoints because this would exceed its budget. The forced eight indices exhaust the count.

The binary-distance tilts realize all eight caps, and an own half-interval contributes exactly ∫₀^{1/2}t dt=1/8 in Euclidean unit continuous normalization. The old hinge on every other fiber is zero. The support denominator is one for D_int and W for D_all, yielding exact normalized minima 1/4 and 1/(4W), with the latter tending to zero.
The frozen locator matches the square example, the sharp point-depth argument and the exact cap minimum in original §6 (12)–(13).

overlap.comparison: The accepted sixteen-fiber n=4,d=1 example already has an explicit sharp-budget 32-cap cover whose real-width objective tends to zero, with a lower estimate for its real width. The present n=2,d=1 square computes the real width exactly, classifies the forced eight half-interval caps and determines both exact minima. Its fixed dimension and optimization conclusions are additional.

The accepted vanishing hinge sequence uses full ambient Euclidean unit normalization and a strict slack budget. The square uses only the same-real-fiber difference body and stays at the exact depth budget.

readability: Here the notation cap budget 1/2 means raw summed fiber length, so the normalized budget is 1/8.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The four-fiber square gives the exact sharp depth and exact minima in both width normalizations. Its real width grows with L while its integer width is fixed.
